h1: Would Your Website Get You Invited to Bid?
seo_title: What Should a Service Business Website Include? | NATA
meta_description: See how buyers judge comparable work, what a project page can prove, and how to decide whether your website needs a rewrite or a rebuild.
section_questions: What makes one project better evidence than another?
What does a buyer actually ask a contractor to prove?
What changes when the buyer is hiring for design judgment?
Should you rewrite one project page or redesign the whole site?
answer_capsule: A service business website should explain the work you take on, show a comparable project, and make it easy to start a conversation about a specific assignment. The strongest project pages tell a buyer what the client needed to protect, what your firm was responsible for, and what you delivered. That gives the person forwarding the link a reason to put your name on the list.
takeaways: **“I found three lobbies. I still don’t know if you’ve worked around tenants.”** Rewrite one project page using a documented constraint and your role. Give the revised page to another reader with the same brief.

**“That occupied renovation is exactly what we need. I only saw it after you sent me the link.”** Give the service page a direct route to the project and label it in the buyer’s language. Repeat the test from the service page.

**“I understood the case. I sent a message about a May start and the person who called asked me to explain the job again.”** Submit a test inquiry and follow it to the person who replies. Check whether the job details survive the handoff and who covers when that person is away.

faqs.question: What if we can’t name the client or show the work?
faqs.answer: Agree on what you can disclose. An approved description can still cover the building type, your role and a constraint you handled. If those details would identify the client, use another project publicly and discuss references through the channels the client permits.

faqs.question: Can we include a project our founder did at a previous firm?
faqs.answer: Credit the firm that held the contract, describe the founder’s own role and check what you have permission to show. Put the experience in the founder’s bio or label it clearly alongside company work. The buyer can then ask which people and capabilities carry over to their project.

faqs.question: What should we track after improving a project page?
faqs.answer: Record whether relevant buyers mention or share the case, whether their inquiries contain enough context to act on, and whether those conversations progress. Keep the counts alongside the period, project type and referral source where known. That makes it easier to tell what’s worth testing next.
